column1: # Token fingerprints of the comment pass, per file.
# sha256 over the ordered `(tag, exact text)` sequence of each file's tokens,
# POSITIONS EXCLUDED and doc-comment tokens skipped. An ordinary `//` comment
# produces no token at all, so this digest is invariant under every edit the
# conservation pass is allowed to make — comment removal, rewording,
# reindentation — and moves on any token insertion, deletion or edit.
# Verify with: zig build fingerprint -- --check briefs/artifacts/m1.E-fingerprint.tsv
# THE REFERENCE IS THE STATE THE CONTENT GATES START FROM, not a fixed point in
# the branch's history. The gates that BUILT this instrument are outside its
# reach by construction — they wrote the rules, the subcommands and the build
# steps, and they corrected code in the open — so a reference taken before them
# reports their declared edits at every later run, and a control that must be
# explained away each time is a control nobody reads. Re-posed here at the last
# commit before the first gate under fingerprint. Measured across that span:
# of the 333 files, exactly ONE token stream moved, `tools/weld_lint/dead_tests.zig`,
# and the whole of its non-comment diff is the two-line per-platform test floor,
# re-derived FROM THE SUITE as the milestone requires. Absorbed, never excused:
# a code edit inside a CONTENT gate still fails this check, which is the point.
# ONE FILE IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: `tools/weld_lint/comment_scan.zig`. It holds
# the pass's own coverage ledger, so each subtree the pass finishes removes an
# entry from it and moves its token stream BY CONSTRUCTION. It is the one
# expected mover; every other moved file is a defect. Excluded here rather than
# tolerated in the report, so a real move cannot hide behind an expected one.
# That exclusion is of a different nature from the re-posing above and does not
# generalise: nothing else may earn a standing exemption.
# Proven in both directions on this tree: stripping all 1110 comment lines from
# a real file and reindenting it left all digests unchanged, while a two-token
# edit in two files was named at exit 1.
